notes.meaning: Peter introduces himself as an apostle, someone chosen and sent with authority by Jesus Christ. He writes to believers living as scattered foreigners across five provinces in Asia Minor, modern-day Turkey. Even though they lived in different places, their real home was in heaven, which made them strangers in a world that did not share their faith.

Peter explains that our salvation involves the whole Trinity working together. God the Father chose believers according to his eternal plan, the Holy Spirit cleanses and sets them apart, and Jesus cleanses them with his blood so they can walk in obedience. Peter prays that God will grant them an overflowing supply of his undeserved favor and peace.

differ.view: God chose his people out of his sovereign, eternal love before creation, not because he foresaw anything good they would do.
God knows all things as eternally present, and his election means he chose that everyone who repents and believes in Christ will be saved from sin.
God looked down through time, saw in advance who would choose to accept his gift of grace, and chose them based on that knowledge.

notes.meaning: Peter praises God the Father for showing immense mercy to sinners. By bringing Jesus back from the dead, God gave believers a brand new spiritual life. This new birth gives us a living hope, a solid confidence that will never die because our Savior is alive.

God is saving an inheritance for his adopted children, which means the eternal home and blessings promised to them. Unlike earthly treasures, this heavenly gift can never decay, become stained by sin, or lose its beauty. It is stored safely in heaven, far beyond the reach of any danger.

While our inheritance is kept safe in heaven, God also guards believers here on earth by his mighty power. He shields our souls through our faith until the final day of history. At that time, Christ will return and reveal the full rescue he has prepared for us.

differ.view: God's power protects true believers so completely that their faith will never fail, ensuring they can never lose their eternal salvation.
God protects believers through their ongoing faith, meaning a person must continue to trust and walk with Christ to retain salvation.

notes.meaning: Believers can be full of joy when looking forward to this salvation, even though hard times cause real sorrow right now. Peter notes that these troubles only last for a little while compared to eternity. God allows trials only when they are needed to help us grow spiritually.

Difficult times put our faith to the test, just as fire melts gold to burn away impurities and prove it is real. True faith is far more precious than gold because gold will eventually perish. When faith passes through hardship, it will bring praise, glory, and honor when Jesus appears.

The readers had never seen Jesus in person, yet they loved him deeply. Even though they could not see him with their physical eyes, trusting in him filled their hearts with an amazing, glorious joy that words could not describe.

differ.view: The salvation received now is a rescue from all sin into a life of holiness. It prepares for eternal salvation and is a pledge of it.
The soul is saved now by faith, which brings us back into peace with God. This salvation comes by faith in God's promise, not by the merit of our works.

notes.meaning: Believers already experience the first fruits of their faith, which is the rescue of their souls from sin. This salvation brings peace right now and guarantees complete deliverance of the whole person in the end.

differ.view: The salvation received now is a present deliverance from all inward sin into complete holiness of heart and life.

notes.meaning: Long ago, the Old Testament prophets foretold the special grace that God would give in the gospel. They studied the scriptures deeply and asked searching questions about this coming rescue. They knew God had a wonderful plan, and they wanted to understand how it would unfold.

The Spirit of Christ was living inside the prophets, showing them ahead of time that the Messiah would suffer and then enter his glory. The prophets tried to figure out when this would happen and what the world would look like when he arrived.

God showed the prophets that they were not writing just for their own day, but to serve future believers. Christian preachers have now announced this good news by the power of the Holy Spirit sent from heaven. This redemption is so marvelous that even holy angels long to look into it.

Peter tells believers to gather up their thoughts and get ready for spiritual action, like a traveler tucking long robes into a belt before running. Being sober-minded means staying calm, alert, and self-controlled. Believers should put their full hope in the grace that Jesus will bring when he appears.
Christians belong to God's family, so they should live as obedient children. Peter warns them not to let their lives be shaped by the selfish desires they used to follow before they knew God.

In the ancient world, pagan gods were often immoral, but the God of the Bible is completely pure and set apart from sin. Because the God who called believers into his kingdom is holy, they are called to reflect his holy character in everything they say and do.
Peter points back to God's command in the book of Leviticus: be holy because I am holy. Since God is the loving Father of his people, his children are expected to resemble him in their daily conduct.

Believers pray to God as their Father, yet they must remember that he judges each person's work fairly without playing favorites. Since their time on earth is short like that of visiting foreigners, they should live with deep reverence and holy respect for him.

To be redeemed means to be bought out of slavery by paying a ransom price. Peter reminds believers that they were freed from an empty, inherited way of living, and no amount of earthly silver or gold could ever buy that freedom.

The ransom price for our rescue was the precious blood of Jesus Christ. Under the Old Testament law, a Passover lamb had to be spotless and healthy to be offered to God. Jesus was completely sinless in himself, making his sacrifice pure and able to wash away our sins.

God chose Christ to be the Savior before the creation of the world, showing that redemption was always part of his plan. Yet Christ came in human flesh during these last days for our sake. Believers can take great comfort knowing that God planned their rescue from all eternity.

Jesus is the one who leads us to trust in God the Father. God confirmed Christ's work by raising him from the dead and honoring him in heaven, giving believers every reason to place their faith and hope firmly in God.

Believers have their souls cleansed from sin by believing and obeying the gospel truth. A pure heart naturally produces sincere, unselfish love for fellow Christians. Peter encourages them to love each other deeply and wholeheartedly.

Christians are able to love this way because they have been born again into God's family. Physical life comes from human parents and eventually dies, but this new spiritual life comes from the living, unchanging word of God.

Peter quotes the prophet Isaiah to contrast human weakness with God's strength. Human beings and all their earthly glory are like grass and wild flowers, which look bright for a short season but quickly dry up and fall to the ground.

Human life quickly passes away, but the word of the Lord stands strong and unchanged forever. Peter explains that this everlasting message is the very good news that was preached to them. Because the gospel never fails, believers can rest their lives securely upon it.
